Subject: Production latency and 5xx spike from Praxis — reserved throughput failing

Marcus / Vanessa —

We started seeing sustained queuing and elevated tail latency from our production inference workloads starting ~08:30 PT this morning. A few quick notes:

- Error rate rose to ~3.7% for our primary endpoint and token-latency p95 drifted from 220ms to ~1.6s.

Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike from Praxis — dedicated pool findings (initial)

Marcus / team / Liam —

Initial findings from a 30-minute triage:
- Dedicated pool GPUs show sustained 98% util on a subset of nodes pinned to Praxis' tenant.
- KV cache hit ratio dropped to 14% for the affected model variant (we saw a sudden change in request prefix distribution).
- Several long-running batched requests (large prompt sets) from a small number of Praxis client instances are monopolizing batch windows, causing head-of-line blocking.
- We see elevated kernel retries on two nodes — one node is reporting OOM-level stalls and kernel back-off signs.

Immediate mitigations executed (10:00–10:03 PT):
- Throttled the largest client IP group to avoid runaway batches.
- Rebalanced a small set of Praxis shards off two overloaded GPUs to warm spare nodes (best-effort).
- Forced fallback to the lighter quantized model variant for non-critical routes to reduce per-token cost and latency.

Still required (actions we recommend now):
1) Emergency burst authorization to give us headroom for a controlled drain (I recommend +40% burst for 2 hours).
2) Purge/compact some KV cache entries for the affected prefix patterns (we'll need a short window).
3) Replace the suspect node (OOM stall) with a healthy node — ops to approve immediate reprovision.

Attachments: kernel_profile_0621.png (screenshot of kernel retries).

I'll continue monitoring; leaving traces open for the bridge.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability

Liam / Praxis team —

Thanks again for the bridge earlier today. Final update and asks:

What we did (summary):
- Emergency +40% burst granted 11:59 PT on 2026-06-20 and used to drain the queued work with minimal additional failures.
- Replaced the node exhibiting OOM stalls and rebalanced Praxis shards across three additional spare GPUs.
- Compacted and warmed KV cache for the dominant prefixes, restoring hit ratio to ~72% within 90 minutes.
- Enabled a temporary stricter per-client batch cap (30% lower) on the top-5 producers to prevent recurrence while we schedule a capacity increase.

Customer impact:
- Error rate fell from 3.7% to 0.3% after mitigation; tail latency p95 returned to ~240ms.

Commercial ask / offer: 
- We recommend a persistent headroom increase (recommended +20% reserved throughput) to avoid repeat events during Praxis' monthly batch windows.
- As committed during the bridge, Redwood will issue a 20% credit for the impacted billing window (details and DocuSign have been sent).

Next steps:
1) Vanessa / Sales to follow up on the reserved throughput change and procurement path (deal DBL-4921).
2) Engineering to schedule a controlled capacity uplift and a long-term shard reallocation audit (Irene to own).
3) Ops to complete the node replacement post-mortem and link to SUP-9142.

Please reply with confirmation that the credit and throughput proposal are acceptable. If Praxis wants an earlier capacity uplift we can prioritize via procurement.

—Marcus
